version.changelog:
**Expanded to a complete financial toolkit with portfolio, trade journal, and watchlist features.**

- New description reflects broader capabilities: live data, portfolio tracking, journaling, screening, and news — no API key needed to start.
- Emphasized portfolio tracking, benchmark performance comparison, and trade rationale journaling.
- Watchlist management now included.
- Clearer messaging: Market data available with no API key; higher limits with free registration.
- General improvements for clarity and highlighting new features for AI-agent use.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mkts-market-data
Version: 1.0.7

The skill provides extensive functionality for interacting with an external financial data API (mkts.io), including reading market data and managing user-specific portfolios, journals, and watchlists. While the `curl` commands are well-formed and target the stated service, the ability to programmatically register for API keys (sending email/name) and modify a user's portfolio holdings (add/delete) on the external service represents significant write capabilities. These capabilities, if misused by a compromised AI agent via prompt injection, could lead to unauthorized modifications of a user's financial data or privacy concerns, classifying it as suspicious due to risky capabilities without clear malicious intent. All interactions are with `https://mkts.io/api/v1` as seen in `SKILL.md`.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only market-data integrator that only uses curl to call mkts.io endpoints and optionally accepts an API key — its requirements and instructions are coherent with its stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (market data, portfolio tracking, news) matches the runtime instructions: all examples are curl calls to https://mkts.io/api/v1 and an optional MKTS_API_KEY. Required binary (curl) is appropriate and proportional.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md contains only API usage examples (GET/POST curl commands) and an optional programmatic registration flow. It does not instruct the agent to read local files, system credentials, or unrelated environment variables. Note: the registration flow POSTs an email/name to mkts.io — if the agent were to register on behalf of a user it would transmit an email address (privacy consideration).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — this is instruction-only. That minimizes installation risk (nothing is downloaded or written to disk).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables; MKTS_API_KEY is declared as optional for higher rate limits, which is proportionate to the service. No unrelated credentials or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-on and is user-invocable; it does not request persistent system privileges or modify other skills. There is no install-time persistence described.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its stated purpose and is low-risk as an instruction-only integration that issues curl calls to mkts.io. Before installing, confirm you trust mkts.io as the external service. If you or the agent register programmatically, be aware the registration POST transmits an email and name — avoid using a sensitive or personal email if you care about privacy. Only provide an MKTS_API_KEY if you control it and understand where it will be stored/used by your agent. Also note the service enforces rate limits (free/basic access) so automated agents should respect those limits.
